title: How to change cursor in Photoshop on Mac: step by step for designers
metaTitle: How to change cursor in Photoshop on Mac: Settings Guide
description: Learn how to change cursor in Photoshop on Mac using the Preferences menu. Fix crosshair issues, brush previews, and tool icon settings for your workflow.
intro: To change cursor in Photoshop on your Mac, navigate to Photoshop > Settings > Cursors in the top menu bar. This menu allows you to toggle between standard tool icons, precise crosshairs, and brush tip outlines.
tldr: Open Photoshop > Settings > Cursors to modify your tool and brush cursor appearance.
Select Normal Brush Tip to see your brush size, or Full Size Brush Tip to see the full extent of your brush.
Check your Caps Lock key if your cursor is stuck as a crosshair, as this is a common accidental toggle.
Use standard tool icons for non-painting tools to keep your interface clean and predictable.

blocks.text: Your cursor in Photoshop is more than just a pointer. It is a visual cue that tells you which tool is active and how it will interact with your canvas. When you work on a Mac, you have granular control over how these cursors appear. You can choose between icons that represent the tool itself, or more precise indicators like crosshairs.

Most users prefer seeing a preview of their brush size while painting. If your cursor is showing as a simple crosshair, you might have changed a setting or accidentally triggered a keyboard shortcut. Customizing these settings ensures that your workflow remains fluid and that you always know exactly where your brush or tool will land.
How to access the cursor preferences menu

The primary way to change cursor in Photoshop is through the Preferences menu. This menu houses all the settings that define how the application behaves on your system. To get there, ensure Photoshop is the active application. Then, look at the top menu bar on your Mac desktop.

items: Click on the Photoshop menu in the top left corner of your screen.
Select Settings from the dropdown list. In older versions of the software, this may be labeled as Preferences.
Choose Cursors from the sub-menu that appears on the right.
A dialog box will open showing all cursor-related options.

blocks.text: Once you have this window open, you can adjust settings for Painting Cursors and Other Cursors. The changes take effect immediately once you click OK. If you are unhappy with the new look, you can always return to this menu to reset your preferences.
Choosing the right brush cursor style

The Painting Cursors section offers the most utility for illustrators and retouchers. You have four main options here. Standard displays the brush icon itself. This is useful if you want to see exactly where the center of the brush is without the outline getting in your way.

Normal Brush Tip is the default for most users. It shows a circle representing the brush size. This circle is based on the soft edges of your brush. Full Size Brush Tip is more accurate. It shows the absolute extent of the brush. This includes the feathered edges, even if they are at low opacity.

Finally, you can check the Show Crosshair in Brush Tip box. This adds a small crosshair to the center of your brush. Many artists find this helpful for precise work where they need to hit a specific pixel every time.

A common frustration for many designers is when their brush cursor suddenly turns into a crosshair. This usually happens because the Caps Lock key was pressed. Caps Lock is a system-wide toggle that forces the cursor into a precise crosshair mode in Photoshop.

If your brush cursor disappears and becomes a crosshair, check your keyboard. If the Caps Lock light is on, simply press the key again to turn it off. Your brush cursor will immediately return to its previous state. This is a deliberate design choice by Adobe to allow for quick switching between a visual brush preview and a precise crosshair.

If you notice your cursor lagging or flickering, the issue is rarely the cursor setting itself. It is often linked to the Graphics Processor settings. You can check these by going to Photoshop > Settings > Performance. Ensure that Use Graphics Processor is enabled.

Photoshop requires at least 8 GB of RAM to run smoothly, though 16 GB or more is highly recommended for professional work. If your system is struggling, the cursor might stutter as you move it across the canvas. Closing other resource-heavy applications can help alleviate this lag.
Common mistakes when changing cursor settings

One mistake is confusing system-wide cursor settings with Photoshop-specific settings. Changing your cursor size in the macOS System Settings > Accessibility menu will affect your entire Mac. It will not change the brush tip size inside the Photoshop canvas. Always make your adjustments inside the Photoshop Cursors menu for the best results.

Another mistake is forgetting to click OK after making changes. If you just close the Preferences window without confirming, your changes will not be saved. Always ensure you press OK to apply the new cursor behavior.

faq.question: Why is my Photoshop cursor a crosshair?
faq.answer: Your cursor is likely a crosshair because the Caps Lock key is enabled on your keyboard. Press Caps Lock once to toggle it off and restore your standard brush cursor.

faq.question: How do I see my brush size in Photoshop?
faq.answer: Go to Photoshop > Settings > Cursors and select Normal Brush Tip or Full Size Brush Tip. This will display a circle representing your brush size on the canvas.

faq.question: Does changing the cursor affect performance?
faq.answer: Changing the visual style of your cursor does not significantly affect performance. However, if your cursor is lagging, check your Graphics Processor settings in the Performance tab of the Preferences menu.

task: Change the cursor appearance in Photoshop
appliesTo: Adobe Photoshop 27.11 and later on macOS

steps.name: Open Preferences
steps.text: With Photoshop open, go to the menu bar and select Photoshop > Settings > Cursors.

steps.name: Select Cursor Style
steps.text: Under the Painting Cursors section, choose between Standard, Normal Brush Tip, or Full Size Brush Tip based on your preference.
steps.tip: Full Size Brush Tip is best for seeing exactly where your brush edges will land.

steps.name: Toggle Crosshair
steps.text: If you need extra precision, check the box for Show Crosshair in Brush Tip.
steps.tip: This is helpful for detailed retouching tasks.

steps.name: Save Changes
steps.text: Click OK to apply the new cursor settings to your application.

troubleshooting.problem: Cursor is stuck as a crosshair
troubleshooting.fix: Press the Caps Lock key on your keyboard to toggle it off.
Check your Performance settings in Preferences and ensure Use Graphics Processor is enabled.
Check your Cursors settings and ensure you have not selected Standard, which hides the brush preview.
